content_units: Best Laptop Match for a CS Student
All three meet your hard requirements:   16 GB RAM  ,   under 1.7 kg  , and   under $1,200  .
Given your priorities, the   Acer Swift Go 14   is the best overall fit because it offers the   strongest battery life   while staying light and comfortably within budget.
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Laptop   Price   Weight   Battery   Best For   Main Tradeoff
1   Acer Swift Go 14   $949   1.32 kg   11 hrs   Best overall balance for student use   Less storage than HP
2   Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5 14   $899   1.46 kg   10 hrs   Best value and stronger CPU-heavy performance   Slightly heavier; battery trails Acer
3   HP Pavilion Plus 14   $1,099   1.49 kg   8.5 hrs   Best if 1 TB storage matters most   Weakest battery for your stated priorities
1) Acer Swift Go 14
-   Why it ranks first:   It best matches your top priority:   battery life  .
- At   11 hours   and   1.32 kg  , it is both the longest-lasting and lightest option here.
- For a CS student,   16 GB RAM + 512 GB SSD   is already a solid baseline for coding, browser tabs, VS Code, light VMs, and typical coursework.
-   Best pick if you want:   long campus days, portability, and no major compromises.
View Acer
2) Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5 14
-   Why it ranks second:   It is the   best value   and may offer the strongest raw multicore performance of the three.
- The   Ryzen 7 8845HS   is attractive if you expect heavier workloads like compiling larger projects, Docker use, or occasional virtualization.
- It still has good battery life at   10 hours  , but it loses to Acer on both   weight   and   battery  , which were your most important constraints.
-   Best pick if you want:   maximum performance per dollar.
View Lenovo
3) HP Pavilion Plus 14
-   Why it ranks third:   It does meet all minimum requirements, but it is the weakest fit for your stated priorities.
- Its biggest advantage is   1 TB SSD  , which is useful if you want lots of local storage for projects, datasets, and dual-boot setups.
- But at   8.5 hours battery  , it falls clearly behind the other two, and battery life was your top need.
-   Best pick if you want:   extra storage more than all-day unplugged use.
View HP
Student-Focused Tradeoff Readout
If battery life matters most
Pick   Acer Swift Go 14  .
It gives you the best chance of getting through lectures, library work, and coding sessions without carrying a charger.
If performance-per-dollar matters most
Pick   Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5 14  .
You give up a bit of battery and portability, but likely gain stronger CPU headroom for demanding programming workloads.
If storage matters most
Pick   HP Pavilion Plus 14  .
The   1 TB SSD   is nice, but for your priority order, the shorter battery life makes it a less ideal student laptop.
Buying Context
Using only the specs you provided, this ranking assumes:
- battery estimates are comparable across brands
- display quality and port selection are not deciding factors
- your priority order is:   battery life first  , then meeting RAM/weight/budget limits, then overall value
